text:
maria_prod_marketing: Quick sync — we need a tight battlecard + webinar narrative for next week's inference econ webinar. Primary opponents: cloud provider managed endpoints, LLM API vendors, and infra runtimes. Goal: crisp rebut lines on predictable unit economics, low tail latency, rollout controls, and private deployment options. Can we list provable claims vs common competitor talking points?

samuel_growth: +1. Focus on two things buyers care about: predictable cost per request and graceful degradation (fallbacks). Also highlight the routing/playbook for when model variants are needed.

avery_field: We should avoid vague words like "cheaper" or "faster" without bench numbers. Eng-ml — can you run a small benchmark (chat + embeddings) using our standard seq lengths? Need p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-1k tokens for 3 model configs.

chris_metrics: I can run that. Which models/seq lengths? Suggest: chat sim: 2 prompts, 1k context avg, 512 generation; embeddings sim: 512 tokens. I’ll run on dedicated-prod and hosted variants to show delta. Expect preliminary numbers in ~36h.

lizzie_content: Drafting hero lines for battlecard:
```
- Serving-first: predictable unit economics, not model ownership
- Deterministic fallbacks: automatic region/model routing to meet SLOs
- Private parity: same APIs + observability in VPC/on-prem
```
Avoid list: "we're better" "most reliable" without SLA/bench link.

maria_prod_marketing: Love the hero lines. Two asks: 1) samuel — can you build 3 single-sentence rebut bullets we can paste into battlecard and field scripts? 2) lizzie — convert hero lines into 2 social posts and the webinar lead magnet copy. 3) chris — bench job + raw numbers + short writeup on test config. ETA EOD Wednesday?

samuel_growth: Draft rebut bullets (working):
- "Predictable unit economics: our autoscaling + batching profiles reduce realized cost per inference vs generic endpoints — see benchmark link."
- "Deterministic SLOs: our routing and fallback policies keep p99 latency stable under contention — automatic model fallbacks avoid noisy neighors."
- "Private parity: run the same APIs in your VPC or on-prem with enterprise controls and KMS/HSM integration."
I'll tighten after chris posts numbers.

avery_field: For webinar narrative, propose a short storyline: 1) myth: model ownership=advantage, 2) reality: serving & routing delivers predictable UX & economics, 3) demo: live failover + cost dashboard, 4) CTA: self-serve trial + Dedicated eval.

chris_metrics: Bench job queued (ci-bench #847). Config summary posted in comment: `model: redwood-open-3b, batch sizes: [1,8,32], seqs: 512/1024`, running on dedicated and hosted variants. ETA ~28–40h. I’ll post p50/p95/p99 + token-cost calc + raw logs link.

ops_bot: deploy_bot: benchmark job #847 started on runner ci-bench-5. Logs: https://ci.internal/847 — results will be posted to /docs/bench-results/847 when complete. :satellite:

maria_prod_marketing: Great. Timelines: we’ll aim to ship battlecard draft by Thu morning, webinar slides by Thu EOD, social posts by Fri. Sam @samuel_growth — will you own the field cheat sheet? @lizzie_content — you own the landing copy and hero social drafts. @chris_metrics — ping here when bench numbers land and include a 1-paragraph explanation of methodology we can paste into the battlecard.

samuel_growth: On it. I’ll also add a quick routing play for SDRs: "If prospect cites latency worries -> show p99 graph + fallback story; If pricing concerns -> show batch/caching case study."

lizzie_content: Will draft and drop two options for hero social: 1) benchmark-led hook, 2) product-story hook. Will tag both so we can A/B in the webinar followups.

maria_prod_marketing: One more note — legal flagged the "private parity" phrase last quarter. Make sure we have an explicit line: "feature parity for inference API surface; optional managed services differ." Keep claims conservative and link to docs.

chris_metrics: Noted. I’ll include test configs and a short "what this does/doesn't prove" section.

maria_prod_marketing: Perfect. Link to the working doc: https://redwood-internal/positioning-lab/positioning-sandbox (please comment in doc, not just thread). Thanks team — we’ll reconvene after bench results. :thumbsup:
